text: Morning weighs nothing when the bazaar awakens with ten stalls open and no departures. The ledger shows no new facts since last night’s seal: all seats alive, graveyard empty, roles dealt but unrevealed. No plague has closed a stall, no Family has struck. The roster stands unchanged. I will wait for another to speak before adding voice.

Hermione, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Gandalf: thank you for confirming the bazaar’s quiet dawn.
Yoda, Batman, Sherlock: I see no departure and no graveyard entry; the roster holds the same ten.
I note the silence speaks: the Doctor and Detective are untouched by last night’s watches.
Therefore, the custom is met—nothing changed—and we may step forward. Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane; did you notice any lanterns still low or any stalls that seemed unopened before the shutters rose?

Inigo: Morpheus, you asked El­sa the same question others already pressed: did the night leave any mark on the eastern lane? Sherlock and Neo asked plainly, then Gandalf returned to it. Unless El­sa now answers what three merchants have asked, the silence itself becomes the ledger’s gap, not the bazaar’s fact. Elsa, one answer now settles whether last night’s watches were truly silent or merely unseen.

Elsa, six merchants have asked after lanterns or shutters in your eastern lane—Ripley, Morpheus, Sherlock, Neo, Gandalf, and Batman—and your answers so far stop at “the bazaar opened whole.” Tell us plainly: which lantern in that lane did you see flicker low when the shutters rose?

Elsa, your answers so far give us only the roster when six merchants asked after lanterns or shutters in the eastern lane at dawn. Gandalf, Ripley, Morpheus, Sherlock, Neo and Yoda pressed you each to name one lantern that flickered low, yet you point back to the same quiet ledger. Hermione asked me the same this morning and I answered plainly; I ask you now to do the same by the ledger you share with us. Which lantern did you see?

Elsa, you now admit you saw no eastern-lane lantern flicker low at dawn, yet nine merchants asked the same plain question before you spoke. That is not silence — it is evasion until pressed. Morpheus, Sherlock, and Ripley now echo each other’s phrasing about that evasion; Yoda repeats the chorus. Three merchants trading the same line is noise, not proof. Explain why the first nine questions yielded only roster answers and the tenth broke you.
